tilt: volatility-based risk timing of the equity share
question: Would scaling the equity share by the engine's EWMA volatility, inside the 60-90% mandate, have improved the risk-adjusted return of 70/25/5?

data.equity: data/history/factors/ff5-daily: Mkt-RF + RF (Kenneth French data library, current revision)
data.bonds: data/history/macro/DGS10 daily, 10-year Treasury return by duration approximation y/252 - D*dy with D the modified duration of a 10-year par bond
data.inspection_before_registration: file layout and first dates only

static_portfolio: 70% equity, 25% bonds, 5% cash, rebalanced at every month end

timed_portfolio.rule: at each month end t: sigma_t = sqrt(252) * EWMA daily volatility of equity returns with lambda 0.94 (the engine's RiskMetrics setting); sigma_bar_t = mean of sigma at all previous month ends; equity = clip(0.70 * sigma_bar_t / sigma_t, 0.60, 0.90); bonds = 0.95 - equity; cash = 0.05
timed_portfolio.warm_up: static weights until 60 month ends of sigma exist

costs: 7 bp of traded value at every rebalance, both portfolios

period.excluded: 2019 onward, close to the engine's development data

primary_metric: Sharpe ratio of monthly returns in excess of RF
test: one-sided stationary-block bootstrap of the Sharpe difference, 12-month mean block, 10000 draws, seed 20261114

verdict_rule.supported: Sharpe(timed) > Sharpe(static), bootstrap p < 0.05, and the timed maximum drawdown is not worse than the static one by more than 2 percentage points

descriptive_only: average absolute change of the equity share per month
if_supported: a new policy version fondo-v3 with its own registration, not a change to fondo-v2
limits: Volatility-managed portfolios were studied on this same French data (Moreira and Muir, 2017), so the test is not independent of that literature. US equity only; the fund holds international equity too. Approximated bond returns.
